## §7.1.1: The Anthropomorphic Pivot & Cognitive Pluralism {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">OPENING OF TEIL B (LEVEL IV CONTINUUM) &amp; STRATUM D (SM, PP. 122–123)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Crossing from Pure Logic (*Teil A*) to Empirical Physics (*Teil B*)
* Chapters 1–6 completed **Teil A**: the universal categorical logic of observation, operadic synthesis, corporate networks, gauge curvature, higher Metroplex towers, and telecentric coalgebras. Yet it contained no physical units or numerical coordinates.
* In §7.1 (SM, pp. 122–123), Heim executes the **Anthropomorphic Pivot** by analyzing the human cognitive baseline (*normal-psychische Konstellation*):
  - Begins with two-valued contradictory predication ($A_0$: $\overline{|\Pi|}_+$ vs. $\overline{|\Pi|}_-$, $\sum h_i = 1$) across a simultaneous **plurality of aspects** $S_{\mathrm{human}} = \bigcup_{i \in I} S_i$.
  - **Qualität (Regional Pluralism):** Color qualia, musical timbre, and affect differ in intrinsic kind; their foundations remain irreducibly plural (**Apodiktische Pluralitäten**, local $\Box_S$).
  - **Quantität (Global Unification):** Spatial extension, duration, and mass admit additive concatenation and ratio comparison under **Mengendialektik** ($\overline{|m|}_+ \equiv {=}$ vs. $\overline{|m|}_- \equiv {\ne} \implies a > b \lor a < b$), converging onto the single overarching **Quantitätsaspekt**.

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

  <video autoplay data-autoplay loop muted playsinline src="media/Ch78_Act1_Anthropomorphic_Pivot.mp4" style="max-height:270px;"></video>
  <div class="video-caption">Manim Act I: Qualitative Apodictic Pluralities vs. Unified Quantitative Mengendialektik</div>
</div>

::: {.carnap-box .fragment}
**Carnap 7.1: Coordinative Definitions & Reduction Sentences**
Following Carnap (*Testability and Meaning*, 1936; 1956), Michael Friedman (*Dynamics of Reason*, 2001), and Bas van Fraassen (2008), abstract theoretical terms ($L_T$) acquire empirical meaning via **coordinative definitions** to an observational measurement language ($L_O$). Restricting $(\Ctx, \Jsyn)$ to module carriers over $\Coeff = [\mathbb{Q} \subseteq \mathbb{R} \subseteq \mathbb{C}]$ and clothing them in physical units via $S_n$ executes this exact coordinative bridge!
:::

:::

::::

::: {.notes}
Welcome to Chapters 7 and 8, which launch Teil B of Syntrometrische Maximentelezentrik and Level IV of our Konstitutionsstammbaum. Why does human science achieve a unified mathematical physics for quantitative magnitudes while qualitative experience remains pluralistic? Because quantitative observables admit additive concatenation and ordering (Mengendialektik) over the algebraic number fields Q, R, and C.
:::

## §7.1.2 & §7.2.1: *Quantitätssyntrix* (SM-28) & Realification Poset $\Coeff$ {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM D/A: QUANTITÄTSSYNTRIX (SM-28) &amp; REALIFICATION FUNCTOR (DEFS. 7.1–7.3, FIGS. 7.1–7.2)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Historical Schema of the *Quantitätssyntrix* (SM Eq. 28, p. 127):**
$$
\mathrm{S}_n ; \widetilde{\mathrm{a}} = \mathrm{R}_n, \qquad \widetilde{\mathrm{a}} = (\mathrm{a}_i)_q, \qquad \quantitaetssyntrix \equiv \widetilde{\mathrm{a}}| = \langle \mathrm{f},\, \mathrm{R}_n,\, \mathrm{m} \rangle \tag{SM-28}
$$
1. **Singularer Metrophor ($\widetilde{a} = (a_i)_q$):** Dimensionless elements in $\mathbb{K} \in \{\mathbb{Q}, \mathbb{R}, \mathbb{C}\}$ (*Zahlenkörper*).
2. **Semantischer Iterator ($S_n$):** Clothes pure numbers with physical dimensions/units $\mathbf{\Lambda} = \operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_n)$, inducing the $n$-dimensional **Semantischer Metrophor ($R_n$)**.
3. **Synkolatorraum ($\Msyn$):** Functional operator $f$ selects $m$ coordinates $R_m \subseteq R_n$ ($\binom{n}{m}$ combinations) to generate a rank-$k$ tensor field ${}^m\bar{A}$ in total bundle space $\Msyn = T^{\otimes k}R_m$ of dimension **$m + m^k$**.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment}
**Definitions 7.1–7.3: Poset $\Coeff = [\mathbb{Q} \subseteq \mathbb{R} \subseteq \mathbb{C}]$ & Realification $V_{\mathbb{R}}$**
 With real dimension factor $d(\mathbb{Q}) = 1,\; d(\mathbb{R}) = 1,\; d(\mathbb{C}) = 2$:
$$
V_{\mathbb{R}} \coloneqq \begin{cases} \mathbb{R} \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}} V & \mathbb{K} = \mathbb{Q} \\ V & \mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R} \\ \operatorname{Res}_{\mathbb{R}}^{\mathbb{C}}(V) & \mathbb{K} = \mathbb{C} \end{cases} \implies U_{\mathrm{quant}}(U_Q) = P^U \cong \mathbb{R}^{3\, d(\mathbb{K}_U)\, n_U}
$$
:::

:::

## §7.2.1–7.2.2: Topos $\Equant$, Dedekind Reals $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{E}}$ & Operad $\Oquant$ {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A: GEOMETRIC MORPHISM (THM. 7.6), DEDEKIND REALS (THM. 7.8) &amp; TENSOR OPERAD (DEF. 7.11)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Prop. 7.4, Def. 7.5 & Theorem 7.6: Quantitative Sheaf Topos $\Equant$**
* Pullbacks in $\CtxQuant$ take the subfield meet $\mathbb{K}_W \coloneqq \mathbb{K}_{V_1} \cap \mathbb{K}_{V_2} = \min(\mathbb{K}_{V_1}, \mathbb{K}_{V_2})$ in $\Coeff$.
* The pullback- and cover-preserving forgetful functor $I \colon (\CtxQuant, \Jquant) \to (\Ctx, \Jsyn)$ induces a canonical **Geometric Morphism of Toposes**:
$$
\pi_{\mathrm{quant}} = \big(\pi_{\mathrm{quant}}^* \dashv \pi_{\mathrm{quant}*}\big) \;\colon\; \Equant \coloneqq \mathbf{Sh}(\CtxQuant, \Jquant) \longrightarrow \Esyn
$$
:::

::: {.carnap-box .fragment}
**Def. 7.7 & Theorem 7.8: Internal Dedekind vs. Cauchy Reals in $\Equant$**
In the internal logic of $\Equant$, $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{E}}$ is the object of Dedekind cuts $(L, U) \subseteq \mathbb{Q}_{\mathcal{E}} \times \mathbb{Q}_{\mathcal{E}}$ satisfying inhabitedness, roundedness, disjointness ($L \cap U = \emptyset$), and **constructive Heyting locatedness**:
$$
\forall q < r \text{ in } \mathbb{Q}_{\mathcal{E}},\qquad L(q) \vee U(r)
$$
The canonical monomorphism $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{Cauchy}} \hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{E}}$ is an isomorphism under internal countable choice or local completeness.
:::

:::

**Defs. 7.9–7.11: Bounded Tensor Operad $\Oquant$ & Isometric $\Oisom$ (Fig. 7.3)**
For color $(m, k)$ denoting $X_{(m,k)} \coloneqq \Gamma_b^0(R_m, T^{\otimes k}R_m)$ ($\|A\|_{C_b^0} = \sup_{y\in R_m}\|A(y)\|_{g_m} < \infty$):
$$
\Oquant\big((m_1,k_1),\dots,(m_r,k_r); (m,k)\big) \coloneqq \mathcal{B}\!\left(X_{(m_1,k_1)} \otpi \dots \otpi X_{(m_r,k_r)},\; X_{(m,k)}\right)
$$
with isometric-equivariant suboperad $\Oisom$: $f(\varphi_* A_1, \dots, \varphi_* A_r) = \varphi_* f(A_1, \dots, A_r)\;\forall \varphi \in \operatorname{Isom}(R_m, g_m)$.
:::

:::

::::

::: {.notes}
Theorem 7.6 establishes a geometric morphism pi_quant between the Quantitative Sheaf Topos E_quant and E_syn. Inside E_quant, Theorem 7.8 constructs the internal Dedekind real object R_E via located cuts (L, U), while Definition 7.11 constructs the colored Banach operad O_quant of bounded multilinear tensor field operations.
:::

## §7.3: Functor $S_n$, Isocline Foliations ($\mathfrak{f}_A$) & Cascade Norm Bounds {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: PARAMETER FUNCTOR (DEF. 7.12), FOLIATIONS (DEF. 7.13) &amp; CASCADE ESTIMATE (THM. 7.16)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="47%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Def. 7.12 (Functor $S_n$) & Def. 7.13 (Isoclines $\mathfrak{f}_A$ & Centers $Z_\alpha$, Fig. 7.5)**
1. **Dimensional Parameter Functor $S_n \colon \DimField \to \Ban$:** Assigns $(\mathbb{K}, \mathbf{\Lambda})$ to $R_n \coloneqq (\mathbb{K}^n)_{\mathbb{R}}$ with weighted norm $\|y\|_{R_n} \coloneqq \max_{1\le l\le n}\lambda_l\|y_l\|_{\mathbb{K}}$.
2. **Regular Isocline Foliation ($\mathfrak{f}_A$):** On $R_m^{\mathrm{reg}} = \{y \mid \operatorname{rank}(d({}^m\bar{A})_y) = d\}$, level sets $\Sigma_c = ({}^m\bar{A})^{-1}(c) \cap R_m^{\mathrm{reg}}$ form a **codimension-$d$ foliation**.
3. **Morse–Bott Field Centers ($Z_\alpha$):** Extrema of $\Phi(A) = \|A\|_{g_m}^2$ decompose into smooth critical submanifolds $\operatorname{Crit}(\Phi \circ A) = \bigsqcup_\alpha Z_\alpha$ ($\dim Z_\alpha \le m$).
:::

::: {.carnap-box .fragment}
**Prop. 7.15 (Musical Pullback $\pi_\gamma^\circledast$) & Thm. 7.16 (Cascade Norm Bound):**
With musical pullback $\pi_\gamma^\circledast(A) \coloneqq \sharp_{g_{m_\gamma}}^{\otimes k_{\gamma-1}} \circ \pi_\gamma^* \circ \flat_{g_{m_{\gamma-1}}}^{\otimes k_{\gamma-1}}(A)$ ($\|\pi_\gamma^\circledast(A)\|_{C_b^0} \le \|A\|_{C_b^0}$) and $\|f_\gamma\|_{\op} \le C_\gamma < \infty$, the iterates $A_\gamma = f_\gamma(A_{\gamma-1}, \dots, A_{\gamma-1})$ satisfy:
$$
\|A_\gamma\|_{C_b^0} \;\le\; \Gamma_\gamma \|A_0\|_{C_b^0}^{D_\gamma}, \qquad D_\gamma \coloneqq \prod_{j=1}^\gamma r_j, \qquad \Gamma_\gamma \coloneqq \prod_{j=1}^\gamma C_j^{\prod_{\ell=j+1}^\gamma r_\ell}
$$
:::

:::

## §8.1–8.2: *Primigene Äondyne* (SM-29), Calculus Functors & SDG {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">CHAPTER 8 OPENING: PARAMETER-TENSORIUM (SM-29) &amp; INFINITESIMAL FUNCTORS (SM EQS. 30–36)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**The *Quantitätssyntrix* as a *Primigene Äondyne* (SM Eq. 29, p. 131):**
> *"Da die Quantitätssyntrix auf Elementen aus algebraischen Zahlkörpern basiert, die kontinuierlich sind, ist sie eine primigene Äondyne."*

$$
\quantitaetssyntrix \equiv \langle \mathfrak{f},\, R_n,\, m \rangle \equiv \widetilde{\mathbf{a}}(x_i)_1^n, \qquad R_n = (x_i)_n, \qquad 0 \le x_i \le \infty \tag{SM-29}
$$
* **Defs. 8.1 & 8.2 ($\ManParam$ & Unital Envelope $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{K}}(\mathcal{M}_n)$):**
  On cornered parameter manifolds $\mathcal{M}_n = (\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n$, the unital base envelope:
  $$
  \mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{K}}(\mathcal{M}_n) \;\coloneqq\; \mathbb{K}\cdot 1_{\mathcal{A}} \oplus \mathscr{S}(\mathcal{M}_n, \mathbb{K}) \;\subset\; C_b^\infty(\mathcal{M}_n, \mathbb{K})
  $$
  intrinsically contains **Fehlstelle $0$** ($\mathbf{0} \in \mathcal{M}_n,\; 0_{\mathcal{A}}$) and **Einheit $E$** ($1_{\mathcal{A}} \colon x \mapsto 1_{\mathbb{K}}$, SM p. 133).
:::

::: {#calc-pane-1 .syn-tab-pane .active}
**1. Infinitesimal Differential Functor $\tilde{\mathrm{d}}|$ (SM Eqs. 30, 30a, 31; Def. 8.3)**
Defined as the limiting corporate subtraction chain as $(\Delta x_i)_n \to \mathbf{0}$:
$$
\tilde{\mathrm{d}}| f \;\coloneqq\; df \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^n \big(\tilde{\partial}_i| f\big)\,dx^i \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial f}{\partial x^i}\,dx^i \;\in\; \Omega_{\mathrm{closed}, b}^1(\mathcal{M}_n) \tag{SM-30}
$$
satisfying the exact Leibniz derivation rule $\tilde{\mathrm{d}}|(f \cdot g) = f\cdot(\tilde{\mathrm{d}}|g) + g\cdot(\tilde{\mathrm{d}}|f)$ (§8.5.1).
:::

::: {#calc-pane-2 .syn-tab-pane}
**2. Poincaré Homotopy Integral Functor $\mathrm{I}_{\mathbf{0}}$ on Corners (SM Eqs. 32–34; Def. 8.3)**
Integrates Whitney-smooth closed 1-forms $\omega \in \Omega_{\mathrm{closed}, b}^1(\mathcal{M}_n)$ along radial rays $\gamma_x(t) = tx$ ($t \in [0,1]$) from the origin $\mathbf{0} \in (\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n$:
$$
\big(\mathrm{I}_{\mathbf{0}}\,\omega\big)(x) \coloneqq \int_0^1 \sum_{i=1}^n x^i \omega_i(tx)\,dt \implies \tilde{\mathrm{d}}|\big(\mathrm{I}_{\mathbf{0}}\,\omega\big) = \omega, \quad \mathrm{I}_a^b(\tilde{\mathrm{d}}|f) = f(\gamma(b)) - f(\gamma(a)) \tag{SM-33}
$$
:::

::: {#calc-pane-3 .syn-tab-pane}
**3. Double-Integral Partial Sieve Composition (Theorem 8.1, SM Eqs. 35, 35a)**
Composing the synkolatively partial integrator ${}_+(y,z)?$ ($\metrophor{y}=\metrophor{z}$) with the metrophorically partial integrator ${}^+(y,z)?$ ($(\underline{f},\underline{p})=(\underline{g},\underline{q})$) on an identical syntrix under $\underline{f}(y_k^2)_1^p = \underline{f}^2$ yields:
$$
{}^+\!\Big({}_+(y, y)?,\, (\;)\Big)? \;=\; \frac{1}{2}\big(\mathbf{y}\widetilde{\mathbf{y}}\big)^2 \qquad \left(\text{Lean 4: }\frac{y\cdot y}{2} + \frac{y\cdot y}{2} = y^2\right) \tag{SM-35a}
$$
:::

::: {#calc-pane-4 .syn-tab-pane}
**4. Carnap 8.1: Synthetic Infinitesimals (Kock–Lawvere) vs. Discrete Metronics**
* **Synthetic Differential Geometry (SDG):** Internal smooth topos line $R$ contains square-zero infinitesimals $D \coloneqq \llbracket d \in R \mid d^2 = 0 \rrbracket$ with $f(x+d) = f(x) + f'(x)d$.
* **Discrete Exterior Calculus (Ch. 10 Metronics):** Finite lattice area step $\tau > 0$ on $\mathbb{M}_\tau^n$ generates the non-linear discrete Leibniz cross-term $\nabla(uv) = u\nabla v + v\nabla u - (\nabla u)(\nabla v)$!
:::

:::

Before the smooth continuum fractures into a discrete metronic lattice in Chapter 10, Section 8.2 proves that Heim's infinitesimal corporate subtraction and addition chains (SM Eqs. 30-36) reproduce exterior differentiation d and Poincaré homotopy integration I_0.

## §8.3.1: Seeley Corner Extension & Grothendieck Nuclearity {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: SEELEY EXTENSION &amp; NUCLEAR VARIABLE SEPARATION (THM. 8.4, FIGS. 8.1–8.2)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.firewall-box}
**Why Naive Corner Extensions Fail II**
For $f(x) = e^{-x}$ on $x \ge 0$, zero extension is discontinuous at $x=0$, while even reflection $e^{-|x|}$ suffers a first-derivative jump ($f'(0^+) = -1 \ne +1 = f'(0^-)$), destroying Schwartz smoothness!
:::

  </p>

::: {.column width="52%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 8.4 ($c_{\mathrm{NUCL}}$): Grothendieck Nuclear Variable Separation on Corners**
Via the continuous linear right-inverse $\mathcal{E}^{(n)} = \bigotimes_{i=1}^n \mathcal{E}_{x_i} \colon \mathscr{S}((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n) \to \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ ($\mathcal{R}_+ \circ \mathcal{E}^{(n)} = \operatorname{id}$), $\mathscr{S}((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^m)$ is a closed complemented subspace of nuclear $\mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}^m)$, inheriting **Grothendieck nuclearity**:
$$
\mathscr{S}\!\big((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^m\big) \;\cong\; \widehat{\bigotimes}_{l=1}^{m,\pi} \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}) \;\cong\; \widehat{\bigotimes}_{l=1}^{m,\varepsilon} \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})
$$
Every kernel $f \in \mathscr{S}((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^m)$ expands into an absolutely convergent separated series $f(x_1,\dots,x_m) = \sum_{j=1}^\infty \lambda_j\, \phi_j^{(1)}(x_1) \otimes \dots \otimes \phi_j^{(m)}(x_m)$ with $\sum_{j=1}^\infty |\lambda_j| < \infty$!
:::

  </p>

</div>

:::

::::

::: {.notes}
How do we rigorously justify Heim's Separation der Variablen on cornered manifolds (R_{>=0})^m? Infinite-dimensional Banach spaces are never nuclear, so projective and injective tensor products differ. However, using Seeley's Vandermonde moment extension across the boundary walls x_i = 0, Theorem 8.4 proves that the Schwartz space S((R_{>=0})^m) is a nuclear Fréchet space where pi- and epsilon-completions coincide!
:::

<script>
window.comb78 = function(n, k) {
  if (k < 0 || k > n) return 0;
  if (k === 0 || k === n) return 1;
  let r = 1;
  for (let i = 1; i <= k; i++) r = r * (n - i + 1) / i;
  return Math.round(r);
};

window.fact78 = function(n) {
  let r = 1;
  for (let i = 2; i <= n; i++) r *= i;
  return r;
};

// WIDGET 1: §7.1.2 & §7.2.1 Realification Poset Coeff & Synkolatorraum (m + m^k)
window.updateQuantSpaceLab = function() {
  const elF = document.getElementById('q-field');
  if (!elF) return;
  let K = elF.value;
  let n = parseInt(document.getElementById('q-n').value);
  let mIn = document.getElementById('q-m');
  mIn.max = n;
  let m = Math.min(n, parseInt(mIn.value));
  mIn.value = m;
  let k = parseInt(document.getElementById('q-k').value);

  document.getElementById('q-n-val').innerText = n;
  document.getElementById('q-m-val').innerText = m;
  document.getElementById('q-k-val').innerText = k;

  let dK = (K === 'C') ? 2 : 1;
  let dimRn = dK * n;
  let dimPU = 3 * dK * n;
  let combNM = window.comb78(n, m);
  let fiberDim = Math.pow(m, k);
  let synkDim = m + fiberDim;

  document.getElementById('q-cards').innerHTML = `
    <div class="stat-card" style="border-left-color:#4169E1;">
      <b style="color:#82aaff;">Realified R_n (d(${K})=${dK}):</b><br>dim_ℝ R_n = <b style="color:#FFD700;">${dimRn}</b> (P^U ≅ ℝ^${dimPU})
    </div>
    <div class="stat-card" style="border-left-color:#20B2AA;">
      <b style="color:#5eead4;">Subspace Choices:</b><br>C(${n}, ${m}) = <b style="color:#FFD700;">${combNM.toLocaleString()}</b> domains
    </div>
    <div class="stat-card" style="border-left-color:#FFA500;">
      <b style="color:#fcd34d;">Synkolatorraum M_syn:</b><br>m + m^k = ${m} + ${fiberDim} = <b style="color:#FFD700;">${synkDim}</b>
    </div>
  `;

  document.getElementById('q-readout').innerHTML =
    `<b>Def. 7.13 Tensor Bundle Total Space:</b> M_syn := T^{⊗${k}} R_${m} has base dim <b>${m}</b> + fiber dim ${m}^${k} = <b>${fiberDim}</b> ⇒ Total Dim = <b style="color:#FFD700;">${synkDim}</b>`;
};

// WIDGET 2: §7.2.1 Internal Dedekind Cut (L, U) Explorer
window.updateDedekindLab = function() {
  const elGap = document.getElementById('ded-gap');
  if (!elGap) return;
  let gap = parseFloat(elGap.value);
  let q = parseFloat(document.getElementById('ded-q').value);
  let r = q + gap;
  document.getElementById('ded-gap-val').innerText = gap.toFixed(2);
  document.getElementById('ded-q-val').innerText = q.toFixed(2);

  const sqrt2 = Math.SQRT2;
  let inL = q < sqrt2;
  let inU = r > sqrt2;

  let xQ = 20 + (q / 2.5) * 380;
  let xR = 20 + (Math.min(2.5, r) / 2.5) * 380;
  document.getElementById('ded-pt-q').setAttribute('cx', xQ.toFixed(1));
  document.getElementById('ded-pt-r').setAttribute('cx', xR.toFixed(1));
  document.getElementById('ded-pt-q').setAttribute('fill', inL ? '#20B2AA' : '#ff6b81');
  document.getElementById('ded-pt-r').setAttribute('fill', inU ? '#FFA500' : '#ff6b81');

  let witness = (inL && inU) ? "Both L(q) ∧ U(r) hold (Straddles α = √2!)" :
                (inL ? "Witness L(q) = ⊤ holds (q < √2)" : "Witness U(r) = ⊤ holds (√2 < r)");
  document.getElementById('ded-readout').innerHTML =
    `<b>Test Pair (q = ${q.toFixed(2)} < r = ${r.toFixed(2)}):</b> <span style="color:#FFD700;">${witness}</span> ⇒ Heyting Locatedness <b>L(q) ∨ U(r) = ⊤_{Ω(U)}</b> Verified!`;
};

// WIDGET 3: §7.3.3 Strukturkaskade Monomial Norm Bound Calculator
window.updateCascadeLab = function() {
  const elM = document.getElementById('cas-m');
  if (!elM) return;
  let M = parseInt(elM.value);
  let r = parseInt(document.getElementById('cas-r').value);
  let C = parseFloat(document.getElementById('cas-c').value);
  let a0 = parseFloat(document.getElementById('cas-a0').value);

  document.getElementById('cas-m-val').innerText = M;
  document.getElementById('cas-r-val').innerText = r;
  document.getElementById('cas-c-val').innerText = C.toFixed(2);
  document.getElementById('cas-a0-val').innerText = a0.toFixed(2);

  let DM = Math.pow(r, M);
  let expC = (r === 1) ? M : (Math.pow(r, M) - 1) / (r - 1);
  let GammaM = Math.pow(C, expC);
  let bound = GammaM * Math.pow(a0, DM);

  let note = "";
  if (a0 === 0) {
    note = ` <span style="color:#20B2AA;"><b>[§7.5.3 Vacuum Stability Check: A₀ ≡ 0 ⇒ A_M ≡ 0!]</b></span>`;
  } else if (r === 1) {
    note = ` <span style="color:#FFD700;"><b>[§7.5.1 Linear Unary Reduction: D_M = 1, Γ_M = C^M = ${GammaM.toFixed(3)}]</b></span>`;
  } else if (a0 === 1.0 && C <= 1.0) {
    note = ` <span style="color:#5eead4;"><b>[Contractive Unit Frame Bound: ‖A_M‖ ≤ 1]</b></span>`;
  }

  document.getElementById('cas-readout').innerHTML =
    `<b>Cumulative Degree:</b> D_${M} = r^M = <b>${DM}</b> | <b>Constant:</b> Γ_${M} = C^${expC} = <b>${GammaM.toFixed(4)}</b><br>` +
    `<b>Thm. 7.16 Cascade Bound:</b> ‖A_${M}‖_{C_b⁰} ≤ Γ_${M} ‖A₀‖^{D_${M}} = <b style="color:#FFD700;">${bound.toFixed(4)}</b>` + note;
};

window.setCasPreset = function(M, r, C, a0) {
  document.getElementById('cas-m').value = M;
  document.getElementById('cas-r').value = r;
  document.getElementById('cas-c').value = C;
  document.getElementById('cas-a0').value = a0;
  window.updateCascadeLab();
};

// WIDGET 4: §8.1.3 & §8.2.2 Infinitesimal Calculus Tab Switcher
window.showCalcTab = function(idx, btnEl) {
  for (let i = 1; i <= 4; i++) {
    const p = document.getElementById('calc-pane-' + i);
    if (p) p.classList.toggle('active', i === idx);
  }
  if (btnEl && btnEl.parentElement) {
    Array.from(btnEl.parentElement.children).forEach(b => b.classList.remove('active'));
    btnEl.classList.add('active');
  }
  if (window.MathJax && window.MathJax.typesetPromise) {
    window.MathJax.typesetPromise().catch(() => {});
  }
};

// WIDGET 5: §8.3.1 Seeley Corner Extension vs Naive Reflection
window.setSeeleyMode = function(mode) {
  const svg = document.getElementById('seeley-svg');
  const box = document.getElementById('seeley-readout');
  if (!svg || !box) return;

  let html = `
    <line x1="20" y1="95" x2="400" y2="95" stroke="#475569" stroke-width="1.8"/>
    <line x1="210" y1="10" x2="210" y2="105" stroke="#FFD700" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="4,3"/>
    <text x="216" y="22" fill="#FFD700" font-size="9.5" font-weight="bold">Corner Wall x₁ = 0</text>
  `;

  // Right side x >= 0: f(x) = e^{-x}
  let ptsR = [];
  for (let i = 0; i <= 50; i++) {
    let x = (i / 50.0) * 2.0;
    let y = Math.exp(-x);
    let sx = 210 + (x / 2.0) * 175;
    let sy = 95 - y * 52;
    ptsR.push((i === 0 ? "M " : "L ") + sx.toFixed(1) + "," + sy.toFixed(1));
  }
  html += `<path d="${ptsR.join(' ')}" fill="none" stroke="#4169E1" stroke-width="3.2"/>`;

  let ptsL = [];
  let colL = "#20B2AA";
  for (let i = 0; i <= 50; i++) {
    let x = -2.0 + (i / 50.0) * 2.0;
    let y = 0;
    if (mode === 'seeley') {
      y = (1.0 - x + 0.5 * x * x) * Math.exp(-1.15 * x * x);
      colL = "#20B2AA";
    } else if (mode === 'even') {
      y = Math.exp(-Math.abs(x));
      colL = "#DC143C";
    } else {
      y = 0.0;
      colL = "#DC143C";
    }
    let sx = 210 + (x / 2.0) * 175;
    let sy = 95 - y * 52;
    ptsL.push((i === 0 ? "M " : "L ") + sx.toFixed(1) + "," + sy.toFixed(1));
  }
  html += `<path d="${ptsL.join(' ')}" fill="none" stroke="${colL}" stroke-width="3" stroke-dasharray="5,3"/>`;
  html += `<circle cx="210" cy="43" r="5" fill="${mode === 'seeley' ? '#20B2AA' : '#DC143C'}"/>`;
  svg.innerHTML = html;

  if (mode === 'seeley') {
    box.style.borderLeftColor = "#20B2AA";
    box.innerHTML = `<span style="color:#20B2AA;"><b>✓ SEELEY MOMENT EXTENSION E_{x₁}f (Thm. 8.4):</b></span> Vandermonde moments ∑ a_k (-2^k)^m = 1 match all derivatives ∂^m f(0⁻) = ∂^m f(0⁺) = (-1)^m across x₁ = 0!`;
  } else if (mode === 'even') {
    box.style.borderLeftColor = "#DC143C";
    box.innerHTML = `<span style="color:#ff6b81;"><b>✗ NAIVE EVEN REFLECTION e^{-|x|}:</b></span> Continuous at x = 0, but first derivative jumps from f'(0⁻) = +1 to f'(0⁺) = -1 (Not in 𝒮(ℝ)!).`;
  } else {
    box.style.borderLeftColor = "#DC143C";
    box.innerHTML = `<span style="color:#ff6b81;"><b>✗ NAIVE ZERO EXTENSION:</b></span> Discontinuous jump from f(0⁻) = 0 to f(0⁺) = 1 at the corner boundary x = 0!`;
  }
};

// WIDGET 6: §8.3.1 Grothendieck Nuclear Series Convergence Lab (Rem. 8.1)
window.updateNuclearSeries = function() {
  const elN = document.getElementById('nuc-n');
  if (!elN) return;
  let N = parseInt(elN.value);
  document.getElementById('nuc-n-val').innerText = `N = ${N}`;

  let partialNorm = 0.0;
  let partialVal = 0.0;
  const eInv = Math.exp(-1.0);
  for (let k = 0; k <= N; k++) {
    let denom = window.fact78(2 * k);
    let lam = (k % 2 === 0 ? 1.0 : -1.0) / denom;
    partialNorm += Math.abs(lam);
    partialVal += lam * (eInv * eInv);
  }
  let exactNorm = Math.cosh(1.0);
  let exactVal = Math.exp(-2.0) * Math.cos(1.0);
  let err = Math.abs(partialVal - exactVal);

  document.getElementById('nuc-readout').innerHTML =
    `<b>Projective Cross-Norm Sum:</b> ∑_{k=0}^${N} |λ_k| = <b style="color:#FFD700;">${partialNorm.toFixed(7)}</b> (Exact cosh(1) = ${exactNorm.toFixed(7)})<br>` +
    `<b>Value at (1,1):</b> Partial Sum = <b>${partialVal.toFixed(8)}</b> vs. Exact e⁻²cos(1) = <b>${exactVal.toFixed(8)}</b> (Error = <span style="color:#20B2AA;">${err.toExponential(2)}</span>)`;
};

// WIDGET 7: §8.3.2 Homometral Polarization & Arity Reduction
window.updatePolarizationLab = function() {
  const elM = document.getElementById('pol-m');
  if (!elM) return;
  let m = parseInt(elM.value);
  let kIn = document.getElementById('pol-k');
  kIn.max = m;
  let k = Math.min(m, parseInt(kIn.value));
  kIn.value = k;

  document.getElementById('pol-m-val').innerText = m;
  document.getElementById('pol-k-val').innerText = k;

  let mult1 = m - k + 1;
  let vars = [`x₁^${mult1}`];
  for (let i = 2; i <= k; i++) vars.push(`x_${i}`);

  let box = document.getElementById('pol-lab-readout');
  if (k < m) {
    box.style.borderLeftColor = "#20B2AA";
    box.innerHTML =
      `<span style="color:#20B2AA;"><b>✓ HOMOMETRAL ARITY REDUCTION (k = ${k} &lt; m = ${m}, Thm. 8.5):</b></span><br>` +
      `Input monomial <b>${vars.join(' · ')}</b> (multiplicities a₁=${mult1}, others=1) factors uniquely via Polarization through <b>F_red(x₁, …, x_${k}) ∈ O_quant(${k}; 1)</b>!`;
  } else {
    box.style.borderLeftColor = "#FFD700";
    box.innerHTML =
      `<span style="color:#FFD700;"><b>★ IRREDUCIBLE HETEROMETRAL TUPLE (k = m = ${m}):</b></span><br>` +
      `All ${m} coordinate inputs (x₁, …, x_${m}) are pairwise distinct; effective arity equals nominal arity m = ${m}.`;
  }
};

// WIDGET 8: §8.3.3 15-to-3 Quantitative Corporate Collapse
window.setQuantCollapseMode = function(mode) {
  const box = document.getElementById('qcol-readout');
  if (!box) return;
  if (mode === 'K') {
    box.style.borderLeftColor = "#FFA500";
    box.innerHTML =
      `<b style="color:#FFA500;">1. Synchronized Coupled Mode Kor_{K} (K := {K_m, K_s}):</b><br>` +
      `Coupling λ > 0 shared coordinates in R_{m_a} ⊞_φ R_{m_b} automatically couples the functional operators f_a, f_b evaluated on those coordinates!`;
  } else if (mode === 'C') {
    box.style.borderLeftColor = "#4169E1";
    box.innerHTML =
      `<b style="color:#82aaff;">2. Synchronized Parallel Mode Kor_{C} (C := {C_m, C_s}):</b><br>` +
      `Disjoint coordinate coproduct R_{m_a} ⊕₁ R_{m_b} forces block-diagonal parallel evaluation of functional operators without cross-modulation.`;
  } else {
    box.style.borderLeftColor = "#FFD700";
    box.innerHTML =
      `<b style="color:#FFD700;">3. Partial Coupled + Composed Mode Kor_{K,C} (Full 2×2 Matrix):</b><br>` +
      `Couples λ shared coordinate channels via K = {K_m, K_s} while keeping the remaining p + q - 2λ uncoupled coordinate channels in parallel composition C = {C_m, C_s}!`;
  }
};

function ensureVideosPlaying() {
  document.querySelectorAll('video').forEach(v => {
    v.muted = true;
    v.playsInline = true;
    if (v.paused) v.play().catch(() => {});
  });
}

function initAllCh78Widgets() {
  window.updateQuantSpaceLab();
  window.updateDedekindLab();
  window.updateCascadeLab();
  window.setSeeleyMode('seeley');
  window.updateNuclearSeries();
  window.updatePolarizationLab();
  window.setQuantCollapseMode('KC');
  ensureVideosPlaying();

  document.querySelectorAll('input[type="range"], select, button').forEach(input => {
    input.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
    input.addEventListener('mousedown', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
    input.addEventListener('touchstart', (e) => e.stopPropagation(), {passive: true});
  });

  if ('IntersectionObserver' in window) {
    const obs = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {
      entries.forEach(entry => {
        if (entry.isIntersecting && entry.target.tagName === 'VIDEO') {
          entry.target.muted = true;
          entry.target.play().catch(() => {});
        }
      });
    }, { threshold: 0.15 });
    document.querySelectorAll('video').forEach(v => obs.observe(v));
  }
}

if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
  document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", initAllCh78Widgets);
} else {
  initAllCh78Widgets();
}

window.addEventListener('load', initAllCh78Widgets);
if (window.Reveal) {
  window.Reveal.on('ready', initAllCh78Widgets);
  window.Reveal.on('slidechanged', initAllCh78Widgets);
}
</script>
